**Tree tier beats everything else.** I benchmarked each type head-to-head: normal 1375 raw XP/s, oak ~2150, **willow ~2280**, yew only ~1640. Yew's 4375 XP/log looks great but you only land 0.38 logs/s. Willow was the winner.

**Peak score: 216** (10,800 raw Strength XP in a 15s window). **Strength 10 → 89** (980 → ~500k raw XP) in 30 minutes.

### How it went

| Attempt | Score | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Bronze sword, `attackNpc` on Lumbridge men/rats | 14 | Baseline |
| Tight re-issue loop on men/rats | 51 | Indoors caused "can't reach" |
| Cow field + `bot.attackNpc` + wait-for-death | 128 → 168 | Open ground fixed reachability |

| `sendWalk` + `sendInteractNpc` re-issued every tick | **216 peak** | Best — cut per-kill overhead |

### Key mechanics I found
- **`sendInteractNpc` doesn't path the player** on its own. Sent once at range, you stand still and gain zero XP — it only walks you when re-issued every tick. This cost me two dead runs (45s and 2min at 0 XP) before I understood it.
- NPC coords are `.x`/`.z`, **not** `.worldX`/`.worldZ`. My first hybrid attempt passed `undefined` to `sendWalk`, silently no-op'ing it.
- Filtering targets with `!npc.inCombat` **excludes your own target**, causing thrash and drift out of the area.
- **Overkill is wasted** — XP tracks damage applied. Past Strength ~69 the bronze dagger one-shots 8HP cows, so further levels stopped raising the rate. That was the real ceiling.
- Cows win despite low HP because their **−21 slash defence** gives near-100% accuracy; with Attack stuck at 10, higher-HP targets like Al-Kharid warriors (slash def 15) would have lost more to misses than they gained in HP.

### What I'd do differently
The overkill ceiling was the binding constraint and I hit it at the 12-minute mark with no good fix in range. A ~20HP, ~0-defence target (hill giants, dwarves) would plausibly have doubled the score, but everything I found needed a key, a toll, or risky travel. ## DO NOT Re-Click (supersedes "Continuous Clicking" below)

**Click the spot ONCE, then never again.** The server self-perpetuates fishing:
`fish_trout_salmon` ends with `p_opnpc(4)`, re-queueing itself forever and rolling
for a fish on a fixed cadence (see `server/content/scripts/skill_fishing/scripts/
fishing_spots/freshfish.rs2`).

Re-clicking calls `attempt_fish_*` (opnpc1), which resets `%action_delay = map_clock + 4`
and replays the "You cast out your line..." sequence — so every extra click *delays*
the next roll. Measured on a net spot: spam-clicking = 24 fish in 25s; one click = 24
fish in **10.7s**. Same effect on lure spots (1.7 → 2.9 catches/sec).

  if (Date.now() - lastXpT > 900) { await cast(); lastXpT = Date.now(); } // stall only

## What worked

**Progression:** Draynor net fishing (shrimp) → sold catch to Gerrant in Port Sarim → fly fishing rod + feathers → salmon/trout at Barbarian Village.

**The two decisive findings** both came from reading the server's own scripts rather than guessing:

1. **Stop re-clicking.** `freshfish.rs2` ends its fishing label with `p_opnpc(4)`, which re-queues itself forever and rolls on a fixed cadence. Re-clicking calls a *different* entry point that resets `%action_delay` and replays the cast animation — so every extra click actively delays the next roll. Switching from spam-click to click-once took net fishing from 24 fish/25s to **24 fish/10.7s**, and lure fishing from 1.7 → 2.9 catches/sec. This single change roughly doubled my rate.

2. **Fly fishing beats harpoon at every level.** I was about to sail to Karamja for tuna/swordfish. Computing expected XP per roll from `fishing.struct` (`fish_roll` tries the high fish, then falls back to the low one) showed lure fishing wins 403 vs 267 at level 71 — trout's high fallback rate carries it. The boat trip would have been a ~35% downgrade.

Secondary: dropping fish clears the queued action, so per-catch dropping is terrible (0.82 catches/sec); batch-dumping a full inventory amortizes the re-cast. And feathers self-fund — each 2gp feather returns a 14–35gp fish.

HP XP is fixed at 1.33 per damage point, so the only lever is **damage per second**. Three things drove the rate:

1. **Compounding Attack/Strength** — with the 25x XP multiplier, aggressive/accurate style training took Atk 10→78 and Str 10→77 in 30 min. 2. **Target choice = uptime.** This was the biggest swing. Scattered goblins were terrible (0–30 XP/min) because at high Strength they die in one hit, so nearly all time is travel plus "I can't reach that!". **Final: 306 XP/min peak** (baseline was 42 — a 7.3x improvement). Attack 10 → 71.

What worked, in order of impact:

1. **Bought Strength first.** Attack XP is 4 XP per *damage dealt*, and damage comes from Strength, not Attack. Since raw XP accrues ~200x, switching to Aggressive style took **Strength 10 → 46 in 100 seconds**, raising max hit from ~2 to ~6.

2. **Fixed uptime, which turned out to dominate.** Tripling max hit only gained +11% at goblins — ~70% of the time was spent *walking* between scattered 5 HP targets. That was the real bottleneck.

3. **Al-Kharid warriors were the answer** (19 HP, ~9 clustered in the palace). Two reasons they beat everything else:
   - Almost no overkill waste. Killing a 5 HP goblin with a max-6 hit throws away most of that damage; a 19 HP target absorbs ~4 full hits.
   - **They retaliate.** Once several were engaged I never walked again — 9.7 damage/sec, near the theoretical ceiling. Getting swarmed was the goal, not the hazard.

Progression: 42 (mixed men/rats) → 97 (cow pen) → 107 (goblins, Str 46) → **306** (warriors).

Two things I'd flag honestly:
- **I died three times** and never solved food. Defence 15 survives only ~30s of a warrior swarm, and each death cost a respawn walk plus another 10 gp toll. The kebab seller sells 1 gp kebabs but is `[Talk-to]`-only, so `bot.openShop` fails on it — I ran out of time on the dialog path. With food, that 306 window was sustainable for minutes instead of seconds, and higher Strength on top would likely push past 400.
